trigger.description: This standard applies to a table when BOTH are true: (1) an active Prefect flow writes to it directly, with no dbt model ever defined against it, and (2) something else depends on it — another Prefect flow reads it, a dbt source block references it, a Lightdash explore/chart queries it, a BI report or dashboard outside Lightdash reads it, or any named external consumer exists. "Touches other things" means a real, identifiable consumer — not hypothetical future use.
trigger.not_triggered: A table with zero downstream consumers — scratch or staging output a flow writes and reads only itself, nothing else touches — is explicitly out of scope and stays uncertified. The moment a second consumer attaches to it, this standard applies and the clock starts: bring it into compliance before merging whatever change created that new dependency, not after.
trigger.owner_of_the_check: The flow's own repo (Prefect code, Ansible-deployed job, etc.) is responsible for knowing whether its output table has consumers and for certifying it once one appears — this is not something OpenMetadata or dbt infra discovers on its own.

certification_gates: lightdash_renders_live (conditional — only where a chart/explore exists against the table)
A named owner (team or individual) is on record for the table

gates.name: discoverable
gates.requirement: The table exists as a searchable OpenMetadata entity before certified=true is set on it. Verify directly — do not assume scheduled metadata ingestion has already picked it up. A newly created or renamed table can lag its own creation by up to one ingestion cycle.

gates.name: certification_tag_matches
gates.requirement: OpenMetadata's own certification field is set and matches this table's certified state, kept in sync in both directions. A stale certification left over after a table stops being certified is the same bug as never setting one — check both sides whenever either changes.
gates.tooling_note: Reuse this org's existing Tier (1-5) classification for business-impact scoping if relevant, but it is not a substitute for the certification field itself — Tier answers how important the table is, certification answers whether it's trustworthy and reviewed.

gates.name: lineage_present
gates.requirement: Real lineage edges for the table's direct upstream (the Prefect flow or source it's landed from) and downstream (every consumer identified by the trigger above) exist in OpenMetadata's lineage graph. Automated ingestion where the landing flow's metadata is published somewhere OpenMetadata ingests it; otherwise a named, tracked manual bridge (link the tracking issue on the table) is the acceptable stopgap — a silent gap is not. A written provenance narrative is not a substitute; prose doesn't get traversed by tooling or show up in impact analysis.

gates.name: lightdash_renders_live
gates.requirement: Conditional, not universal: only applies where a Lightdash chart or explore exists against this table. Where one does, it must render live and non-empty, cross-checked against the real underlying data — not just "the explore compiles with no errors."

not_required_yet:
Fully automated dbt-artifact-style lineage ingestion for Prefect flows — not live anywhere in the org as of this writing. A named manual bridge is the acceptable stopgap per the lineage_present gate above; this does not relax once that automation exists for a given flow, the same way dbt.yaml already commits to for dbt models.
Retroactively auditing every existing Prefect-landed table for whether it already has an undeclared downstream consumer. This standard governs new and changed dependencies going forward; a backfill audit is tracked separately, not assumed done by this file existing.
